background_notes.fact: For a C¹ map v:I→ℝ^m on an open real interval, d(v·v)/ds=2v·v'. In particular, if |v(s)|=1 throughout I, then v(s)·v'(s)=0 at every s∈I. For fixed x, H002 and H004 give such a map v(s)=u(x,s) on I=(0,∞), with v'(t)=u_t(x,t).

background_notes.justification: Restrict each smooth component of u to the time coordinate line. The ordinary one-variable product rule and finite-sum differentiation applied to v·v=Σ_{k=1}^m v_k² give Σ_k 2v_k v'_k=2v·v'. Since |v|²=v·v=1 on the interval, its derivative is zero; division by 2 yields the identity. These rules apply locally at every t>0 within the open interval.
